mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle on the copied DNA was most worthwhile: the time-strip showed how chromosome copies reach opposite nuclei, while the cytoplasm remains connected.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle was less clear to me. The picture showed fibres growing from centrosomes, but I didn't understand what the motor arrows were doing.

surprise.text: I was surprised that each copied DNA helix has one old strand and one new strand.

arbitrary.text: The spindle parts were named in the goal, so I could combine them without really understanding how centrosomes help build it. The pairing made sense as a direction, but not fully as a process.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because seeing how these stem cells later become different kinds of cells sounds interesting. The clear pictures helped, though I'd want more explanation of unfamiliar structures.
